answer: Only 64% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. Because the falcon ledger attributes every share, the knoll audit exposes the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, thus it burns the beacon fee twice and still divides one payout. That is 9 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
